benchmark.cacheState: Fresh process/application caches; OS file cache uncontrolled; no persistent reduced-texture cache.
benchmark.memoryMeasurement: Linux wait4 measures the entire exporter lifetime. getrusage measures the small native monitor and Node harness. Acceptance uses their conservative peak sum plus 1 MiB tail reserve, and samples their contemporaneous process-tree RSS every second when available. Native threads are included. If /proc sampling is unavailable or namespace-inconsistent, the exact lifetime conservative peak sum remains the acceptance measurement. A failed current-RSS call uses the harness OS lifetime peak conservatively and is excluded from contemporaneous sampling; V8 heap/external values remain measured and unavailable ArrayBuffer bytes are null.

limitations: The first render of an unseen world is 81.100 seconds and does not meet 60 seconds.
The 14.085-second replay uses a pre-existing world-specific hybrid tape; the first 113.471-second preparation includes its first PNG.
The tape includes native ordered commands plus exact precomputed residual cells, and is bound to the input world, resources, source version and export scope.
Pixel equivalence is to the pinned static fullbright renderer, not full live Terraria lighting and entities.
Memory is a conservative sum of complete-lifetime process peaks, including the harness and native monitor plus 1 MiB.
Dependencies and world-independent native compilation are excluded. Correctness checks run outside cold timing; input/tape verification is included in replay.
Only cold generation was repeated locally for the final shared-arena runtime. Full preparation and replay in earlierMeasuredStage belong to e2ca3ae and must not be relabeled as f7ac441 measurements.
The final f7ac441 full cold, preparation and replay are additionally measured on the remote runner and archived separately.
All runs use fresh processes. OS page cache is uncontrolled; CPU model is unavailable in this local sandbox.
The arena statistics are captured while the last native output remains readable; normal renderer disposal subsequently releases its final lease.
Component retained-buffer caps are not the complete process RSS; the benchmark uses conservative lifetime RSS including harness and native monitor.
